arxiv.title: GOFish: Full Field-of-View Gaussian Splatting and Mesh Extraction
arxiv.star_quote: GOFish improves PSNR over the best prior method by 2.28 and 1.97 dB, respectively.
arxiv.headline: 魚眼画像から180度を超える広視野角の3D Gaussian Splattingとメッシュ抽出を実現
arxiv.what: 魚眼レンズ特有の歪みや周辺減光を考慮したGOFishを提案し、180度を超える視野角（FoV）のレンダリングとメッシュ抽出を同時に行います。Calibrated Mip FilteringとWide-Angle Appearance Modelingを導入することで、広角画像特有のボケや光量低下が再構成品質に悪影響を与えるのを防いでいます。
arxiv.enables: 200度以上の広視野角ベンチマークにおいて、従来手法をPSNRで最大2.28dB上回り、LiDARなしで衝突判定が可能なデジタルツインをリアルタイムで構築できます。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来のGaussian Splattingはピンホールカメラモデルに依存していましたが、ロボットや自動運転で一般的な魚眼レンズの全視野を直接扱えるようになった点が重要です。
tags: コンピュータビジョン

arxiv.title: Learning Without Clocks: Partition-Invariant Neural Network
arxiv.star_quote: We construct the minimal TM layer, a learnable, provably Lipschitz generalization of the Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator
arxiv.headline: サンプリングの間隔や順序に依存しない、時間連続的なイベント駆動型ニューラルネットワーク
arxiv.what: イベントカメラ等の非同期データを扱うため、イベント間の時間差を閉じた形式で記述し、処理順序や時間刻みに依存しないPartition-Invariant Neural Networkを提案しました。同時発生イベントの交換可能性（Commutation）を数学的に証明し、これを満たすClock-Free Event（CFE）レイヤーを構築しています。
arxiv.enables: 音声コマンド認識などのタスクにおいて、従来の加法的な状態更新モデルを最大30.6ポイント上回る精度を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来はイベントデータを固定時間のフレームに区切る必要がありましたが、本手法は時間解像度の変化に対してロバストであり、物理的な時間スケールに直接対応した学習を可能にします。
tags: ニューラルネットワーク

arxiv.title: CADENCE: Distributional Next-Transaction Forecasting for Business Cash-Flow Underwriting
arxiv.star_quote: CADENCE improves one-day timing accuracy by 93.3% and next-event F1 by 6.7%
arxiv.headline: 中小企業のキャッシュフロー予測をカレンダー対応のTransformerで高精度化
arxiv.what: 取引をトークンとして扱い、次回の支払い金額とタイミングの確率分布を予測するカレンダー対応モデルCADENCEを開発しました。外部ラベル付け器と固定されたテキストエンコーダを組み合わせることで、履歴が短い取引先に対してもセマンティックな情報を活用して予測を行います。
arxiv.enables: 既存のFFTベースのベースラインと比較して、1日のタイミング精度を93.3%向上させ、融資承認率を18.2%向上させつつ損失率を維持することに成功しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 不規則なスケジュールを持つ中小企業の収支を、解釈可能な確率分布として出力できるため、金融の実務における与信判断の自動化に直接貢献します。

arxiv.title: ParaTTT: Parallelizing Test-Time Training Layers with Deep Memories
arxiv.star_quote: We introduce ParaTTT (PTTT), an algorithm for parallelizing arbitrarily deep nonlinear memories by iteratively refining estimates of the inner-loop gradient trajectory.
arxiv.headline: テストタイムトレーニング層の並列化により、非線形メモリの推論と学習を大幅に高速化
arxiv.what: テストタイムトレーニング（TTT）層の非線形メモリ更新を、隠れ層の勾配軌跡を反復的に推定することで並列化するParaTTTを提案しました。順方向パス、Gated Delta Ruleパス、逆方向パスの3段階をチャンク並列で実行することで、シーケンシャルな更新を回避しています。
arxiv.enables: 従来のTTT-MLPと比較して、4Kコンテキストでの軌跡評価を32倍、340Mパラメータモデルの訓練を4.9倍高速化しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: Mamba-2などの線形再帰モデルよりも表現力が高い非線形メモリを、Transformerに近い効率で並列実行できる道を開いた技術です。
tags: テストタイムトレーニング

arxiv.title: Optimal Regret for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning
arxiv.star_quote: we first develop Ascent-gossip, which combines an online compression strategy with a Chebyshev recursion and attains a faster consensus rate than existing compressed gossip methods.
arxiv.headline: 通信効率の高い分散型オンライン学習において最適なリグレット下界を達成
arxiv.what: 通信コストを抑えるためのメッセージ圧縮を伴う分散型オンライン凸最適化において、Ascent-gossipという新しいコンセンサス手法を提案しました。チェビシェフ再帰とオンライン圧縮を組み合わせることで、既存手法よりも高速にネットワーク全体の情報を共有します。
arxiv.enables: 凸関数および強凸関数において、理論的な下界と一致する（対数因子を除き最適な）リグレット境界を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 分散環境での機械学習における通信ボトルネックを解消しつつ、理論的に最良の学習効率を保証した点が重要です。

arxiv.title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents
arxiv.star_quote: We propose World Reward Models (WRMs), which learn from real execution results to choose directly which candidate will perform better, without predicting any intermediate outcome.
arxiv.headline: 実行結果そのものではなく、報酬の優劣を直接予測する「World Reward Models」
arxiv.what: プログラム生成エージェントにおいて、コードの実行結果（出力）を予測する代わりに、複数の候補のうちどちらが優れた報酬を得るかを直接予測する手法（WRM）を提案しました。ForeCriticという9Bパラメータのモデルを構築し、実行結果のペアを用いて学習させています。
arxiv.enables: エージェントのタスク実行時間を4.4〜7.5倍短縮しつつ、成功スコアを維持または向上させることに成功しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 重いコード実行をシミュレートする「世界モデル」の代わりに、意思決定に特化した「報酬モデル」を用いることで、LLMエージェントの探索効率を劇的に改善します。

arxiv.title: Explore Where It Matters: Targeted Exploration for Efficient Rover Adaptation
arxiv.star_quote: TERRA reaches approximately 90% slope-climbing success within five trials under severe out-of-distribution pretraining conditions
arxiv.headline: 報酬に関連するモデル誤差を優先的に探索し、惑星探査ローバーの不整地適応を高速化
arxiv.what: オンライン適応フレームワークTERRAを提案し、報酬に直結する予測誤差がどこで発生するかを予測して探索をガイドします。シミュレーションで学習した世界モデルを、展開時に得られる少数のデータで報酬加重損失を用いて更新します。
arxiv.enables: Marsシミュラント（火星模擬土壌）の斜面において、実機のローバーが3〜5回の試行で適切な locomotion（移動）を獲得することに成功しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 試行錯誤の回数が限られる極限環境において、タスク遂行に不可欠なデータのみを効率的に収集してモデルを修正できる実用的な手法です。

arxiv.title: Verifiable LLM-Guided Focal SMT Solving for Quantified Arrays
arxiv.star_quote: LinguaArray solves up to 69.1% of instances and increases solved-instance counts by 105%--397%
arxiv.headline: LLMの推論をSMTソルバの検証プロセスに組み込み、配列論理の解法能力を向上
arxiv.what: LLMに問題のセマンティックな構造を分析させ、重要な項（Semantic Focus Set）を提案させることでソルバをガイドするLinguaArrayを提案しました。LLMの出力はそのまま信じるのではなく、従来のSMTソルバが検証可能な範囲でのみ使用されます。
arxiv.enables: 既存のSMTソルバ単体では解けなかった問題を含め、解決可能なインスタンス数を105%から397%増加させました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: LLMの「直感」をソルバの「厳密な検証」と組み合わせることで、信頼性を損なわずに形式的手法の限界を拡張しています。

arxiv.title: How Much Should a VLA Trust Its Reasoning? Step-Level Guidance as a Measured Action-Value Function
arxiv.star_quote: sets a new state of the art among published methods: 8.135159 rater feedback score
arxiv.headline: VLAポリシーの推論ステップに対する信頼度を、Q学習ベースのガイダンスで適応的に制御
arxiv.what: 推論トレースを生成するVision-Language-Action (VLA) モデルにおいて、推論が行動決定に与える影響度（ガイダンスの重み）を状況に応じて調整するQ-adaptive guidanceを提案しました。重みの選択をマルコフ決定過程と見なし、批判者（Critic）を用いて最適な重みを推定します。
arxiv.enables: Waymoの自動運転ベンチマークにおいて、固定の重みや従来の強化学習手法を上回るSOTA（最先端）のフィードバックスコア8.13を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: LLMの「推論（思考）」が常に正しいとは限らないという前提に立ち、推論をどれだけ行動に反映させるべきかを理論的に最適化した点が特徴です。

arxiv.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
arxiv.comment: 29 pages, 9 figures, 14 tables. Project page: https://ephemeral6.github.io/awm-site/. Ancillary files contain the Lean 4 model of the running example lp85
arxiv.star_quote: Algebraic World Model (AWM), a framework that turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models supporting formal reasoning.
arxiv.headline: 未知の環境の法則を数学的な世界モデルとして抽出し、Lean 4で到達不可能性を証明
arxiv.what: Algebraic World Model (AWM) を導入し、環境との対話から実行可能なPython仮説を生成し、それを圏論的変換によって簡略化した上でLean 4形式の証明に変換します。これにより、単なるシミュレーションを超えた厳密な形式論理による推論を可能にします。
arxiv.enables: 既存のLLM（Claude Opus等）が解けなかった「到達不可能なゲームレベル」において、全試行でカーネルチェック済みの不可能性証明を生成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: AIが未知のルールを自ら形式化し、数学的な厳密さを持って「何が不可能か」を証明できることを示した重要な成果です。

arxiv.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
arxiv.comment: 84 pages, 19 figures, 3 tables. Code: https://github.com/srikrrish/operator_learning (tags neopic-arxiv-v1, neopic-arxiv-v1-nufft); analysis scripts: https://github.com/NEOPIC-framework/neopic-paper-scripts
arxiv.star_quote: a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid
arxiv.headline: 格子を使わず粒子データを直接扱うニューラルオペレータによるプラズマシミュレーション
arxiv.what: プラズマ粒子のシミュレーションにおいて、格子（グリッド）を介さず粒子の測度から直接電磁場を計算するNEOPICを提案しました。粒子ノイズをエリアシングなしで扱い、計算量は粒子数に対して線形（O(Np)）にスケールします。
arxiv.enables: 2次元および3次元の電磁プラズマ解析において、トレーニング期間の2倍の時間ステップまで安定して計算を継続できることを確認しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来のParticle-in-Cell手法における格子の依存性を排除し、物理現象のノイズを正則化として利用する新しい物理学習の枠組みを提供します。
tags: ニューラルオペレータ

arxiv.title: GAAC: Lossless KV Compression for Bandwidth-Efficient LLM Inference on Personal Devices
arxiv.star_quote: GAAC achieves 1.405-1.407$\times$ lossless BF16 KV compression.
arxiv.headline: LLM推論時のKVキャッシュを可逆圧縮し、メモリ帯域のボトルネックを解消
arxiv.what: 指数の冗長性を利用したGAAC（Group-Adaptive Additive Codec）という可逆圧縮システムを提案しました。BF16形式の値を1ビットも損なうことなく圧縮したまま保持し、アテンション計算時にタイル単位でオンザフライ復元を行います。
arxiv.enables: BF16のKVキャッシュを約1.4倍に可逆圧縮し、NVIDIA GPU上でデコード速度を最大1.15倍、スループットを13-29%向上させました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: メモリ容量が限られる個人用デバイスやエッジ環境において、精度を落とさずに長文脈のLLM推論を高速化できる実用的な技術です。

arxiv.title: Deogen: Automatic Benchmark Generation for Reasoning over Policies
arxiv.star_quote: DeoGen, a scalable, automatic, and parametrizable benchmark generator for deontic reasoning.
arxiv.headline: 政策やルールに基づく法的推論能力を評価するベンチマークの自動生成フレームワーク
arxiv.what: DeoGenは、ルールを1次論理に形式化し、決定木から多様な判定シナリオを自動生成するツールです。正解が確定しているケースだけでなく、情報不足により判定を保留すべきケースも組み込むことで、LLMの「知ったかぶり」を評価できます。
arxiv.enables: 最先端のLLMでも、情報不足の場合に適切に回答を控えることができる割合は22-40%にとどまることを明らかにしました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 法的判断などの規制が厳しい分野でのLLM評価を、人手を使わずに大規模かつ体系的に行えるようにします。

arxiv.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
arxiv.star_quote: We turn the hypothesis into a theorem. First, we prove a \emph{Platonic Representation Theorem}
arxiv.headline: マルチモーダルモデルが「プラトン的な世界表現」に収束するための理論的証明
arxiv.what: 異なるモダリティ（画像とテキスト等）のモデルが同じ世界表現を学習するという「プラトン的表現仮説」を、Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) を用いて定理として証明しました。適切な「良い視点（ペア）」があれば、LLMのような次トークン予測よりも効率的に共有表現を学習できることを示しています。
arxiv.enables: 次トークン予測に比べて42倍少ないサンプル数で同等の位置合わせを実現し、画像ペアなしでImageNet-100のゼロショット精度64%を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: モデルを巨大化させるだけでなく、データの「視点」の与え方が表現の質の決定要因であることを理論と実験の両面で示した重要な知見です。

arxiv.title: Unlimited OCR Works 2
arxiv.star_quote: Unlimited OCR 2 achieves 7.0$\times$ and 5.6$\times$ per-step speedups over Full Attention and R-SWA
arxiv.headline: 100ページ超の長尺文書を一定のメモリコストで高速に解析するOCR 2.0技術
arxiv.what: Unlimited OCR 2は、Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA) を採用し、デコーダのアテンション範囲を一定に制限します。これにより、文書が長くなっても計算コストやメモリ消費が増大しない「人間が現在見ている箇所だけを書き写す」ような動作を実現しています。
arxiv.enables: 100ページ規模の解析において、フルアテンション比で7倍の高速化を達成し、長尺文書解析ベンチマークでSOTAを記録しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 従来のモデルでは不可能だった数百ページにわたる一括の文書解析を、一般的なGPUメモリの範囲で、かつ高速に実行可能にします。

arxiv.title: Well-Specified and Well-Tested? Assessing SWE-bench-Style Datasets with a Self-Evolving Agent
arxiv.star_quote: ExLabel maintains an evolving experience bank that distills cross-instance knowledge
arxiv.headline: コーディングエージェントの評価データセットを、LLMベースの経験学習で自動クリーニング
arxiv.what: SWE-benchなどのソフトウェアエンジニアリング用データセットの品質を向上させるため、ExLabelという自己進化型アシスタントを提案しました。過去の評価経験を「経験バンク」に蓄積し、タスクの明確さやテストの網羅性を文脈に応じて適応的に判断します。
arxiv.enables: Pythonおよびマルチリンガル環境において、既存のクレンジング手法を最大49.9%上回るF1スコアで高品質な学習データを抽出しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 実世界のバグ修正データセットには不正確なラベルが多く含まれますが、これを高精度に自動修正・抽出することで、モデルの学習効率を底上げします。

arxiv.title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
arxiv.star_quote: AB-Attention skips 89--92\% of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.8--3.6$\times$ as much
arxiv.headline: 動画生成Transformerのアテンションを9割削減し、推論速度を2倍以上に高速化
arxiv.what: AB-Attentionは、追加の訓練を必要とせずにアテンション計算を疎（sparse）にする手法です。クエリブロック内でのクラスタリング（IBCS）と確率加重サンプリング（SIP）により、重要なキー/値のみを選択して計算することで、全結合アテンションを精度良く近似します。
arxiv.enables: Wan2.1やHunyuanVideoなどのモデルにおいて、アテンションの89-92%をスキップしながら、2.23倍の高速化と最大4.4dBのPSNR向上を達成しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 計算コストが膨大な動画生成DiTにおいて、品質を維持（あるいは向上）させたまま劇的に計算量を削減できる実用的な手法です。

arxiv.title: Low-Bit GDN Recurrent-State Quantization: Global Gradient-aware Allocation and Pure-Write Sliding Windows
arxiv.star_quote: GGA allocation alone improves over STEPQuant@4 by 19.48/29.84 percentage points.
arxiv.headline: 線形アテンションの再帰状態を低ビット量子化しつつ、長文推論の劣化を抑制
arxiv.what: Gated DeltaNetなどの再帰状態を低ビットで保持するためのGGA（勾配考慮型ビット割り当て）とPW（純粋書き込みスライディングウィンドウ）を提案しました。重要なヘッドに優先的にビットを配分し、最新の情報を量子化誤差のないFP8ウィンドウで保持してから圧縮状態にマージします。
arxiv.enables: Qwen3.5-9Bにおいて、従来の量子化手法をタスク平均で41.21ポイント上回り、量子化による「無意味な長文出力」の抑制にも成功しました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 長文推論においてボトルネックとなるKV状態を大幅に圧縮しつつ、推論品質を維持するための重要な手法です。

arxiv.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
arxiv.headline: EMAコピーを用いた特徴量の一致により、少数ステップの画像生成品質を向上
arxiv.what: Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) は、生成器のEMA（指数移動平均）コピーの特徴量を用いて、生成分布と参照分布のモーメントを強制的に一致させる手法です。外部の画像エンコーダを必要とせず、自身の生成プロセスから得られる統計量を利用します。
arxiv.enables: 1〜2ステップの画像生成において、LongText-BenchでSOTAを達成し、プロンプトへの忠実度と詳細の再現性を大幅に向上させました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: 蒸留ベースの高速な画像生成モデルにおいて、追加の計算リソースを抑えつつ分布のズレを補正する効率的なアプローチです。

arxiv.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
arxiv.headline: 外部データなしでモデル自らが学習信号の低下を検知し、タスクを更新する自己改善法
arxiv.what: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) において、モデルが自身の学習ログから「現在のタスクから学べるものがなくなった時期」を自動判断するA-RSIを提案しました。モデル自身がプログラムを介して生成した問題と、そのプログラムが導く客観的な正解を用いて学習を継続します。
arxiv.enables: 外部データや人間によるラベルを一切使わずに、11種類のベンチマーク平均スコアを57.77から61.05へ向上させました。
arxiv.why_it_matters: モデルがいつ、何を新しく学ぶべきかを自律的に判断する「自己改善の自律化」に向けた重要なステップです。

arxiv.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
arxiv.headline: 全モダリティを単一のエンコーダとスキーマで構造化データに変換する全能パーサー
arxiv.what: 文書、画像、音声、動画のすべてを、共有の時空座標系と単一のスキーマ（OmniSchema）で構造化データへ変換するYoutu-Parsing-Omniを開発しました。OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation (OSAD) という自己進化型の学習手法により、10種類の解析タスクを統合しています。

arxiv.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
arxiv.headline: 潜在空間の3D Gaussianをメモリとして活用し、無限の世界をリアルタイムに生成
arxiv.what: L3G-Worldは、3D Gaussian Splattingをビデオ生成DiTの潜在空間に組み込んだ世界モデルです。新しく観測された領域にのみGaussianを生成・更新することで、生成距離に関わらずメモリ効率を維持し、VAEの再エンコードなしで高速にレンダリングします。

arxiv.why_it_matters: インタラクティブなゲームやシミュレーションにおいて、過去に訪れた場所の整合性を保ちながら、広大な世界を遅延なく生成し続けることができます。

hf.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
hf.abstract: Training a spatial VLM to answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. When post-training emphasizes one readout, improvements can therefore concentrate on that interface while transfer to others remains weak or even degrades; we call this observed specialization interface lock-in. ChronoReplay addresses it by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes, retaining source-native targets, and balancing supervision across families. Under the same observation access, a single ChronoReplay checkpoint improves OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench together, including a 13.41-point gain on OST-Bench, and achieves the highest three-benchmark mean among the supervision settings compared here. Same-data controls further separate the ingredients of this transfer: answer serialization redistributes gains across OST and UCS, family-balanced learning improves over ordinary joint SFT and natural turn weighting, and chronological replay exceeds a shifted-order control by about 2.41 OST points across two paired seeds. Adaptive frame selection then changes evidence access while keeping the trained model fixed, providing an additional inference-time gain at lower visual cost. Streaming spatial performance depends on what distinctions supervision preserves, how heterogeneous histories are organized during learning, and what causal evidence inference makes available at test time.
hf.title_ja: ChronoReplay: ストリーミング空間知能のための単一インターフェースの限界
hf.summary_ja: 異種混合の空間的教師あり学習を時系列順に再生し、複数の空間表現間でバランスを取ることで、特定機能の強化による他機能の劣化を防ぎ、空間理解力を向上させる。

hf.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
hf.abstract: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous tasks at the same node, Creator abstracts their common requirements into simplified, verifiable simulated worlds for capability learning, while evaluation on original tasks measures transfer. Along this capability tree, Explorer progressively evolves reusable capability modules through selective inheritance, forming a Harness tree whose validated updates accumulate across iterations within a fixed topology. The resulting Harnesses specialize in different capabilities, motivating a Capability-Aware Harness Router that uses public task information to select compatible module configurations from the tree. Our evolved Harnesses improve mean performance by 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two real-world embodied tasks.
hf.title_ja: The Trinity: マルチモーダルエージェントのための能力駆動型再帰的自己改善
hf.summary_ja: 生成、探索、進化の3つの役割を通じて環境構築と評価指標の更新を結合し、高コストな手動環境構築に頼らず、複雑化するタスクに合わせたエージェントの自己改善を実現する。

hf.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
hf.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. We propose Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), combining Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale. Extensive experiments across search, tool-use, and automation tasks with 4B and 30B-A3B models demonstrate consistent gains over strong RL baselines.
hf.title_ja: 長期LLMエージェントのためのマルチスケール方策最適化
hf.summary_ja: トークン単位とターン単位の両方で報酬を適切に割り当て、重要度サンプリングを組み合わせることで、長期的なタスクを扱うエージェントの学習効率と性能を一貫して向上させる。

hf.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
hf.abstract: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in their realized executions. Structural-support selection allocates the resulting experience, while parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning preserves the semantic interaction as the unit of training weight. This reframes trajectory generation as the deliberate construction of learnable interaction experience, rather than the collection of successful trajectories. Across five Qwen3 scales, Trajectory2Gym improves Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL at every tested scale, increasing the equal-weight three-benchmark mean by 16.9-29.8 percentage points. The gains are strongest in stateful and multi-turn interaction, where later decisions depend on earlier observations and feedback. Our results suggest that scaling tool-use agents depends not only on collecting more successful trajectories, but on constructing interactions whose dependencies are represented and whose decisions are learnable from the agent's visible history.
hf.title_ja: Trajectory2Gym: ツール利用エージェントのための意思決定根拠に基づく構成的対話合成
hf.summary_ja: 未学習の構成的構造を持つ実行可能な対話を構築し、エージェントが可視化可能な履歴のみに基づく行動から教師データを得ることで、効果的なツール操作の学習を実現する。

hf.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
hf.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used to solve real-world problems, and their effectiveness depends on both the underlying models and the harnesses that support their operation. However, most existing benchmarks focus on model capabilities and overall agent performance, with limited attention to the evaluation of agent harnesses. To address this gap, we introduce TraceTrial-Bench, which organizes harness reliability into seven components covering context, execution, governance, lifecycle, observability, tools, and verification. We construct 95 expert-level, mechanism-oriented tasks with executable or state-based ground truth to support semantically equivalent comparisons while preserving the native behavior of each harness. We design a Trajectory Tracing (TT) module to capture agent execution traces and introduce a two-layer evaluation framework that separately assesses agent performance and harness reliability. In addition, we design a Multi-source Evidence Acquisition (MEA) module to provide evidence from the agent context, harness, and execution environment for LLM-based evaluation, and develop a Failure Attribution (FA) module that uses explicit mechanism chains to support attribution at the run level. Across 4 harnesses, 9 models, and 95 tasks, our evaluation of 3,420 runs yields macro-averaged harness scores ranging from 59.8% to 72.0%, while 31.1% of runs achieve task success despite failing at least one harness criterion. TraceTrial-Bench provides an auditable and reproducible foundation for comparing agent harnesses, diagnosing their failures, and studying how harness design interacts with model behavior.
hf.title_ja: Trial by Trace: 信頼性と失敗原因特定のためのAIエージェント実行基盤の評価
hf.summary_ja: コンテキストや実行など7要素に分類した95の専門タスクを用い、モデル単体ではなく、ツールや検証を含むエージェント実行基盤自体の信頼性を定量的に評価可能にする。

hf.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
hf.abstract: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.
hf.title_ja: ビデオを通じた世界の読み書き、共有、対話
hf.summary_ja: ビデオを潜在的な世界の部分的な投影と捉え、「読み、書き、共有、対話」の4つの操作軸で、基盤モデルと世界モデルの発展を統合的な視点から整理するサーベイ論文。

hf.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
hf.abstract: One-step and few-step text-to-image generation must accurately render the details specified in the prompt despite limited opportunities for refinement. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) uses score differences to bring the generated distribution closer to a reference distribution. Following prior work, we estimate this difference with internal velocity branches, avoiding a separate fake-score network. We ask whether an explicit moment constraint improves this learned score supervision. A decomposition of the reverse-KL field into a Gaussian moment component and a non-Gaussian residual identifies statistics that can be constrained explicitly. We introduce Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM), which retains the full DMD correction and matches feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations using the generator's exponential-moving-average (EMA) copy, requiring no external feature encoder. Experiments use full-parameter and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) tuning on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B. At two network evaluations, IDM reaches 94.25% and 90.20% on Chinese and English LongText-Bench, the highest scores among the compared methods at this budget. Controlled ablations show gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with an external DINOv2 encoder across the five reported metrics. Code is available at https://github.com/inclusionAI/IDM.
hf.title_ja: 本質的分布マッチング
hf.summary_ja: 生成分布と参照分布のモーメントを明示的に拘束する手法を導入し、少ないステップ数でもテキストの指示に忠実な詳細を持つ画像を生成できる、効率的な蒸留法を提案する。

hf.title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
hf.abstract: Streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE) is essential for latency-sensitive applications. However, current causal systems face two coupled gaps. First, standard benchmarks fix the number of speakers at two and ignore the near-/far-field interference, reverberation, and sudden noise of real scenes. Second, high-performance causal architectures are too heavy for edge deployment. Lightweight alternatives try to reclaim capacity by repeatedly invoking a small separator, which offsets the savings. To address the first gap, we release RealSSA, a realistic AVTSE benchmark consisting of RealSSA-Sim and RealSSA-Real. RealSSA-Sim provides controllable simulated scenes with 1--5 dynamic near-field interfering speakers; scenes with far-field interference additionally include 10--15 far-field interfering speakers. RealSSA-Real provides a held-out real-recorded evaluation set. To address the second gap, we propose Falcon, a causal AVTSE method. Its Separator performs multi-scale time-frequency separation in a single encoder--decoder pass. We train Falcon with an encoder-space speaker contrastive loss. This loss suppresses near-field leakage at zero inference cost and transfers across backbones. Falcon achieves state-of-the-art extraction quality on RealSSA-Sim, LRS2-2Mix, LRS3-2Mix, and VoxCeleb2-2Mix. Compared with the causal AV-TFGridNet baseline, it cuts parameters by 91.9%, computation by 20.2 times, and GPU inference latency by 11.1 times. Code and demo are available at https://cslikai.cn/Falcon/.
hf.title_ja: 実世界の音響シーンにおける効率的なストリーミング視聴覚対象話者抽出
hf.summary_ja: 多人数や騒音、残響を伴う現実的な視聴覚データセットを公開し、計算負荷を抑えつつエッジデバイスでの実行に適した、低遅延な話者抽出用軽量アーキテクチャを提案する。

hf.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
hf.abstract: Vision-language models are shifting from offline passive understanding toward online proactive interaction. However, prevailing methods largely rely on explicit requests while miss the implicit user intent (e.g., "where should I click next?" while a user navigate a website), meanwhile fail to update the state simultaneously as user requests might update continuously. These limitations make them less suited to intent-aware interaction in practical. To address these challenges, we introduce StreamVibe-Bench, a new benchmark serving as testbed for user intent interaction, with 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples spanning explicit, implicit, and dynamic intents. Building on this benchmark, we develop StreamVibe-VL, a streaming proactive model that infers implicit user intents from continuous observations and dynamically tailors its interactions as these intents evolve. We further introduce StreamVibe-Harness, which maintains user intents as persistent states with a fleixble lifecycles via a hierarchical memory to track the latest user intent and environmental state. Our experiments reveal three key findings: (i) StreamVibe-VL preserves strong general video understanding while improving response timing and answer quality by 10.7% over other baselines; (ii) existing proactive models remain limited in understanding user intent and deciding when to respond, especially under implicit and dynamic intents; and (iii) StreamVibe-Harness further improves response consistency and adaptation over sustained interaction, resulting in a 12.3% gain in proactive interaction.
hf.title_ja: StreamVibe: 変化するユーザー意図に対応する能動的ビデオエージェント
hf.summary_ja: 明示的な指示だけでなく、継続的な対話で変化する潜在的な意図を理解する能力を測るベンチマークを構築し、動的な環境下で能動的に応答するビデオエージェントを実現する。

hf.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
hf.abstract: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Through a large-scale evaluation across multiple benchmarks and model backbones, we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value. Taking RAG as a reference, we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termed memory benefit and memory tax. These gains and losses arise because memory process changes how the raw information is organized and accessed. We view such changes as the double-edged deviations from the raw history. They are originally designed and introduced to benefit the task, for example by reorganizing facts or distilling preferences, but some may also remove or obscure evidence, giving rise to memory tax. Since memory benefit reflects the expected gains of its design, we then focus more on the overlooked memory tax, study how it arises from the system and evaluation side, and generalize the concept to more application scenarios of memory. We hope the notion of memory tax can provide a new lens and shift more attention from standalone performance to the net value of memory, informing more reliable memory designs and evaluations. We will open-source the code and results to the community. Project Page: https://hexuan21.github.io/MemoryTax/
hf.title_ja: メモリ税：エージェントメモリの純価値を解剖する
hf.summary_ja: 専用のメモリシステムが単純な検索（RAG）を下回る「メモリ税」を分析し、情報の再編成が検索精度に与える利点と損失を切り分けてエージェントメモリの真価を評価する。

hf.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
hf.abstract: Recursive self-improvement requires models not only to acquire useful training experience, but also to decide when their current experience has ceased to be useful. Existing methods often focus on what experience to generate next, while paying less attention to when fresh experience should be introduced. Many also construct training targets through self-consistency or majority voting, making supervision depend on the model's own uncertain predictions. We address these two questions separately: training dynamics determine when to acquire new experience, while the answers to new tasks remain independently checkable. A-RSI monitors reward variation and accuracy in training logs to refresh a task pool when its learning signal declines, without consulting validation or test scores. A static library of model-authored programs produces multimodal questions and derives their reference answers; we specify the task-generation contract, automatically verify chosen properties of the reward and refresh rules, and separately audit the generated answers. The training loop uses no external training examples or human-written answer labels. On the primary eleven-benchmark suite, A-RSI raises the performance average from 57.77 to 61.05 with 800 fresh tasks.
hf.title_ja: A-RSI: ゼロデータ・マルチモーダル自己改善のための適応的タスク更新
hf.summary_ja: 学習ログの報酬変化と正解率を監視し、経験の有効性が失われたタイミングで新たなタスクを自動生成・更新することで、外部データなしでの再帰的な自己改善を効率化する。

hf.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
hf.abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.
hf.title_ja: PDRVLA: 物理動力学表現を備えた視覚・言語・行動モデル
hf.summary_ja: 動画生成による遅延を回避しつつ、軽量な物理動力学モジュールで未来の状態を予測・表現することで、物理法則への理解を深めたロボット行動生成を低遅延で実現する。

hf.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
hf.abstract: Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-form executable workflow synthesis into the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinate sub-agents through sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent through supervised fine-tuning on distilled trajectories, followed by refinement on examples filtered for unsupported premises, biased verification, and information-flow defects. All sub-agents remain fixed, separating orchestration learning from executor capability improvement. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, scientific question answering, and multi-hop retrieval, DynaFlow achieves 88.08% overall accuracy in Forced mode, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.90 percentage points with the same Qwen3.5-27B backbone. Workflow analysis finds more explicit use, verification, and refinement of upstream outputs after training, highlighting cross-stage information flow as a key dimension of multi-agent orchestration.
hf.title_ja: DynaFlow: 形式に縛られないマルチエージェント連携の学習
hf.summary_ja: 固定された連携構造ではなく、メインエージェントが必要に応じて連携用プログラムを自律生成・実行することで、多様なタスクに柔軟に適応するマルチエージェント環境を実現。

hf.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
hf.abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning in language models, but scalar outcomes provide coarse supervision over response trajectories. Self-distillation offers denser token-level guidance by comparing an unassisted policy with a feedback-informed self-teacher, yet the teacher evolves with the student, creating unstable targets and motivating additional regularization. We introduce Function-Space Policy Optimization (FSPO), a single-policy framework that combines current privileged adaptation with function-space temporal consolidation. FSPO stores sparse historical next-token distributions as fixed temporal targets, providing temporal separation without maintaining a persistent teacher model. It further introduces privileged disagreement correction to explicitly suppress locally overvalued actions, reliability-adaptive grounding that strengthens reference supervision when self-generated evidence repeatedly fails, and quality and coverage-aware temporal memory that retains verified behaviors and improves privileged demonstrations. Across reasoning and tool-use benchmarks, FSPO achieves the highest average accuracy under a 5-hour training budget, improving over the strongest baseline by approximately 4% points on average while reducing peak memory from about 70 GB to 56 GB on Olmo3-7B-Instruct.
hf.title_ja: 方策最適化のための関数空間時間的自己蒸留
hf.summary_ja: 過去の次トークン分布を固定ターゲットとして保存し、現在のモデルを適応させることで、追加の教師モデルなしで学習の安定性を保ちつつ、検証可能な報酬によるRLを改善する。

hf.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
hf.abstract: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. In this work, we develop this measure-based view of benchmark evaluation. This perspective allows us to identify and formalize two central failure modes: measure mismatch, where the benchmark difficulty distribution differs from the intended difficulty distribution, and coverage gaps, where uncovered regions along the difficulty axis prevent benchmarks from detecting meaningful localized training progress. We propose two diagnostic metrics that capture these two failure modes and provide rigorous theoretical guarantees. Empirically, we analyze 25 popular benchmarks spanning 7 domains using carefully estimated item difficulties. Our results show that many benchmarks implicitly overweight certain difficulty regions, so their leaderboard conclusions should be interpreted with caution; others leave substantial portions of the difficulty axis uncovered, limiting their ability to monitor the model improvement process. Finally, we turn diagnosis into action by introducing BenchFill, a simple difficulty-targeted item rewriting algorithm that effectively reduces local coverage gaps.
hf.title_ja: ベンチマークは難易度に関する経験的尺度である
hf.summary_ja: ベンチマークを難易度の分布として定義し、意図した難易度との乖離や評価の空白領域を特定する指標を提案することで、モデルの能力向上をより厳密に検出可能にする。

hf.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
hf.abstract: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators, InteractiveWorld lets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduce InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable, state-based rewards. Experiments with 12 frontier MLLMs show they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.
hf.title_ja: InteractiveWorld: 高性能な対話型MLLM構築のための検証可能な人間中心環境
hf.summary_ja: ウェアラブル端末越しの視覚を模した環境を提供し、ユーザーの物理的な作業（料理等）をMLLMがリアルタイムで支援・指導できるかを検証可能な閉ループ評価環境を実現。

hf.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
hf.abstract: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed by diffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research on interactive world generation.
hf.title_ja: Hy-Nomas: 自由形式の対話的世界生成に向けて
hf.summary_ja: 自由なテキスト指示とカメラ制御に基づき、過去の文脈を保ちながら可変長の動画セグメントを生成できるビデオ世界モデルを提案し、複数ターンの対話的な動画生成を可能にする。

hf.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
hf.abstract: Recent test-time training (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient test-time adaptation method for scientific discovery. We introduce Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide subsequent discovery without updating model weights. To have a clean comparison, we evaluate TTME and TTT under the same discovery framework, replacing only the test-time adaptation method. Our evaluation shows that TTME outperforms TTT on all five mathematical tasks, while reducing computational cost by 82.8-84.6% in FLOPs and 47.7-58.4% in runtime. These results establish TTME as an effective and computationally efficient alternative to TTT in the evaluated discovery settings.
hf.title_ja: 科学的発見においてテスト時メモリ進化はテスト時トレーニングを凌駕できるか？
hf.summary_ja: オンラインの重み更新を行うテスト時トレーニング（TTT）の代わりとして、外部メモリに経験を蒸留して更新し続ける手法を提案し、計算効率を保ちつつ科学発見能力を向上させる。

hf.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
hf.abstract: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.
hf.title_ja: ワークエージェント：システム、能力、および最適化
hf.summary_ja: 情報生成から業務実行へと進化するエージェントを、実行環境と結合したシステムとして定義し、業務の継続性や開放性の観点からデジタルワークの遂行能力を分類・整理する。

hf.title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
hf.abstract: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image. Visual token pruning methods partially relieve this burden by removing part of the visual tokens, but they lose the removed information and still process the remaining image at every step. To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compare LLaDA-V's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%. We therefore propose LOWN, a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask. LOWN predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. We further observe that the need for the image differs across benchmarks, so LOWN's adaptive decision is needed rather than a fixed schedule. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average. LOWN also generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally with visual token pruning, and runs under key-value caching for further efficiency gains. Code and project page are available at https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/
hf.title_ja: 必要な時だけ見る：効率的な拡散VLMのための証明書誘導型視覚ルーティング
hf.summary_ja: デコードの各ステップで画像の必要性を判定し、不要なステップでの画像処理をスキップすることで、生成品質を維持したまま計算コストを大幅に削減する推論手法を提案する。

hf.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
hf.abstract: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies. Retaining past interactions alone does not ensure that agents can infer habits and apply them appropriately. We introduce HABIT-Bench to evaluate how well agent memory systems infer habits from weak evidence and apply them to later requests. We construct synthetic user histories from task-oriented dialogue data and controlled habit graphs. The histories span hundreds of sessions across food, finance, software, and travel. Four-choice tasks assess agents' ability to infer user habits and apply them appropriately. They include temporary exceptions, changes in habits, and suggestions that users have not accepted. Sampled tasks undergo independent human review. We evaluate eight memory methods with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.3-Flash. The best-performing memory method achieves 33.61\% macro accuracy across the four domains. Performance remains limited even when annotated evidence is supplied directly. These results expose a persistent gap between access to past interactions and the ability to infer and appropriately use user habits.
hf.title_ja: HABIT-Bench: エージェントメモリにおける長期的な弱い証拠からの習慣推論の評価
hf.summary_ja: 断片的な対話履歴からユーザーの潜在的な「習慣」を推論し、後の要求に適切に応答できるかを測る、数百セッションにわたる長期的なメモリ評価用ベンチマークを構築。

hf.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
hf.abstract: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. We introduce VibeVideoBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on code-driven video generation. Its 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese span 12 categories, from data stories and music-driven pieces to classroom lessons and paper explainers; each asks an agent, running in its native harness inside a sandbox with no image or video generation model, to deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour. Evaluation is hierarchical and evidence-based: program checks of the delivery spec, about 13k task-specific rubric checks traced to the requirements they enforce, and five quality dimensions anchored per task, scored by three VLM judge panels. Across nine frontier agent systems and 2,151 scored rollouts, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 rank first and second with both the judges and human annotators, and the strongest system satisfies every core requirement on 76.3% of tasks. Delivery is a second axis: counting missing videos as zero changes the ranking, and three quarters of the lost videos are final renders that started too late, ran too slowly or never started, a failure of how agents plan their hour. Agents build their own rendering pipelines and inspect their own frames, yet how much they look does not predict quality. The judges' ranking of the systems closely matches blind human preferences.
hf.title_ja: VibeVideoBench: コード駆動型ビデオ生成におけるマルチモーダルエージェントの評価
hf.summary_ja: 正確な図表や数式、音の同期が必要な動画生成を「コード生成と実行」のみで完結させる能力を評価する239のタスクを公開し、視覚生成モデルに頼らないエージェントを評価する。

hf.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
hf.abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. We build a scalable training system that unifies distributed world-model search with asynchronous real-robot execution, forming a self-reinforcing cycle: real-world experience continually sharpens the world model, and a sharper world model in turn drives further policy improvement. We term the world-model side of this cycle test-time physics grounding, a capability that hand-built physics simulators lack: while the world model serves as the training environment, real transitions from the policy it trains correct its dynamics through a lightweight LoRA pipeline. Experiments on three challenging real-world tasks show that Rollback improves success rates over the strongest baseline by an absolute 10.67%, 11.11%, and 11.85% on block extraction, ball tossing, and tabletop curling, respectively, while achieving more stable improvement throughout training. Although initialized from teleoperated demonstrations far below human level, Rollback surpasses the average success rate of human players on both ball tossing and tabletop curling within 8 hours of training.
hf.title_ja: Rollback: 方策向上のための世界モデルにおける経験のバックトラッキング
hf.summary_ja: 世界モデルを過去の分岐点まで巻き戻し、異なる行動をとった場合の結果を比較検証することで、成功の要因を特定し効率的にロボットの方策を改善する学習フレームワーク。

hf.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
hf.abstract: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. Instead, the effective bit budget of discrete indices emerges as a key determinant of downstream performance. However, existing quantizers eventually saturate as additional codebooks contribute progressively less semantic information. As one approach to alleviating this saturation, we introduce Factorized Vector Quantization, which quantizes complementary, fixed-dimensional views of the visual feature with symmetric parallel codebooks. It continues to improve at larger bit budgets, ultimately matching continuous visual representations in multimodal understanding. Trained on industrial-scale multimodal data, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance among discrete-representation models, outperforming UniAR and Emu3-Chat by 22.8% and 59.2%, respectively, on a nine-metric average. To our knowledge, it is also the first discrete-representation model competitive with strong continuous-representation models such as Qwen3-VL, including on fine-grained OCR tasks. We further identify the key principles and a practical recipe enabling this competitiveness. These results and insights support the potential of discrete visual representations to underpin large-scale native multimodal foundation models. Code and models are available at https://github.com/hustvl/FVQ
hf.title_ja: 離散トークンは視覚信号のセマンティックロスレスな表現となり得るか？
hf.summary_ja: 量子化誤差と意味理解能力は必ずしも相関せず、有効なビット予算が重要であることを示し、離散視覚トークンが連続表現と同等以上のセマンティック性能を持ち得ることを実証。

hf.title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
hf.abstract: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. Early subject-to-video (S2V) methods condition on a single reference image and must therefore infer the subject's unseen appearance and geometry as the viewpoint changes. To address this limitation, recent methods extend S2V to multiple reference views, providing more information about the subject from different viewpoints. However, they do not explicitly specify the 3D structure that connects these observations. In addition, existing training data do not guarantee that viewpoint changes preserve the same underlying 3D subject. We present OmniShowcase, built on two components: (i) a fully automated data synthesis pipeline that produces training videos along diverse camera trajectories, with viewpoint variation driven by underlying subject geometry, even spanning full 360-degree orbits; and (ii) a geometry-conditioning method that provides the video model with a turntable of surface-normal maps reconstructed from the reference views without requiring temporal alignment with the generated frames. We construct Showcase-4K, a corpus of 3D-asset-based videos covering twelve camera motions across 88 trajectory configurations with reconstruction-derived surface-normal conditioning, and ShowcaseBench, a held-out evaluation set with the source meshes and camera parameters used to render each video. Experiments show state-of-the-art subject identity and 3D consistency while maintaining competitive video quality and motion. Project page: justin4ai.github.io/OmniShowcase
hf.title_ja: OmniShowcase: 多視点画像からの全方位的な被写体一貫性ビデオ生成
hf.summary_ja: 複数の参照画像から3D構造を明示的に構築し、未学習の背面なども含め全方位から見た被写体の一貫性を維持したまま、カメラワークに追従する高品質な動画生成を実現する。

hf.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
hf.abstract: Agentic recommendation pursues shopper goals through sequences of context-dependent decisions. Developing and evaluating such policies requires faithful recommendation world models that capture both the interactive shopping environment and users' behavioral responses over long interactions. Existing resources rarely provide long-horizon, fine-grained real-user trajectories or support trajectory-level evaluation and offline validation against production A/B results. We introduce UserArena, a real-world e-commerce interactive benchmark containing 64,729 session trajectories from 11,010 users, spanning 566,102 items and 13 action types. UserArena pairs these trajectories with an interactive environment and supports offline validation against outcomes from a controlled production A/B test, enabling five-level evaluation from output validity and local decisions to sequential behavior, personalization, and outcomes. To improve simulator fidelity over these long-horizon interactions, we further propose On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD), which uses trajectory-level intent to provide dense teacher targets on student-generated rollouts. Experiments show that OPTD achieves the strongest overall fidelity among the evaluated simulators under UserArena's evaluation protocol and most closely reproduces the production policy effect in offline simulation.
hf.title_ja: UserArena: 長期ショッピングエージェントのための対話型ユーザーシミュレーション評価
hf.summary_ja: 実世界の膨大なECデータと対話環境を組み合わせ、ユーザーの長期的な行動特性を再現するシミュレータを通じて、動的に変化する目標を追うエージェントを評価可能にする。

hf.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
hf.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose language model activations into sparse features, but prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request can redistribute activity across them. A feature change observed on one transformed prompt need not recur, and even a recurring change need not affect a downstream computation. We introduce the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS), which identifies large feature responses that recur in a consistent direction, and evaluate the resulting supports on variants excluded from selection. Across 27 pretrained SAEs spanning eight language models, the tested prompt transformations produce a reproducible redistribution profile on these excluded variants. We then separate recurring representation change from signed readout contribution and decision failure. For a fixed linear readout, an exact decomposition shows how response magnitude, readout coefficients, directional alignment, and the clean margin determine downstream consequences. In two frozen safety readouts, combining RSS support erosion with the full clean margin yields recurrent failure AUROCs of 0.935 and 0.958 using median supports of 20 and 19 features, compared with 0.965 and 0.964 using full erosion. RSS therefore provides a way to identify recurring sparse representation changes and quantify their contribution to a downstream readout without equating representation change with failure. Code is available at https://github.com/OpenSAE/Redistribution-Sensitivity-Score
hf.title_ja: スパースオートエンコーダにおける表現の再分配
hf.summary_ja: プロンプトの細かな表現変更で活性化する特徴量が変化する現象に対し、一貫して反応する特徴を特定する指標（RSS）を提案し、LLM内部の表現構造の再現性を分析する。

hf.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
hf.abstract: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears only 47.7% of levels and completes all five levels in just 23.3% of tasks, highlighting the difficulty of sustained learning from experience for existing frontier LLMs. As such, the dataset can also be used to post-train LLMs to strengthen their continual learning capabilities.
hf.title_ja: 継続学習試験：LLMエージェントにおける長期間の自己改善と経験学習の評価
hf.summary_ja: 専門的な12業務領域の120タスクを用い、単一タスクの遂行能力ではなく、蓄積した経験を活かしてより難易度の高いタスクへ適応・改善し続ける能力を定量的に測定する。

hf.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
hf.abstract: Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy context to signal candidate completion. At the control level, a single VLA executes all subtasks with vision-only perception and native keyboard-and-mouse actions. To mitigate interference between heterogeneous GUI and non-GUI interactions, we introduce regime-specific RMSNorm branches and separate mouse-movement token embeddings. We also train the VLA through world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environment feedback to improve reliability and recovery. HiSTEVE achieves state-of-the-art atomic-task performance, scoring 85.0% on MineStudio Bench and a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, while also completing long-horizon tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch like human players.
hf.title_ja: HiSTEVE 1.0: オープンワールドゲーム用人間インターフェースVLAエージェント
hf.summary_ja: Minecraftにおいて、長期的な計画立案と、APIを使わない人間と同じ画面操作（視覚運動制御）を階層的に組み合わせることで、自律的に複雑なタスクをこなすエージェントを実現。

hf.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: One Encoder, One Schema, All Modalities
hf.abstract: We present Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time, providing a perception layer for agents that read, locate, and cite evidence across modalities. Its design rests on one encoder for every modality and one schema for every task. Youtu-Omni-Encoder, initialized from a pre-trained language model to strengthen text reading, encodes all modalities with shared weights in a unified space-time coordinate system, and a few fusion layers let video frames attend to concurrent audio, bringing cross-modal fusion and temporal alignment into perception itself. OmniSchema unifies the outputs of all ten parsing tasks, allowing a single self-evolving post-training procedure, OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation (OSAD), to provide a shared token-role-based objective across tasks. In each round, the model is trained on its own rollouts against token-level targets from a reference-conditioned copy of itself, which is then refreshed with the trained weights, so that the parser and its supervision co-evolve. With a single 5 B-parameter checkpoint, Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves state-of-the-art performance on OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.96 Overall) and leads all open-weight models on OmniParsingBench (75.08 Avg.), with its advantage concentrated on audio and video. It also achieves the best overall chart-parsing score (95.02) and the highest exact chemical-fingerprint agreement among compared systems, and matches a dedicated optical-music model in character-level transcription of typeset sheet music while staying far ahead of general-purpose systems. Code and model weights are publicly available.
hf.title_ja: Youtu-Parsing-Omni: 一つのエンコーダとスキーマで全モダリティを処理
hf.summary_ja: 文書、画像、音声、動画を共通の時空間座標系でエンコードし、単一のスキーマで構造化データへと変換することで、全モダリティを横断的に理解・引用できる知覚層を実現する。
